summary: A brick mansard-roofed house on a concrete pier in the water at New London Harbor's mouth, lit in 1909 after nearly two decades of Lighthouse Board requests.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements: first keeper (Norwich Bulletin 11 Nov 1909 names Captain Bloom; USLHS roster lists Petty); fog signal 1911 (NRHP) vs siren from opening (LighthouseFriends); automation 1978 (NLMS page) vs 1987; ownership 2014 vs 2015; Clark term 1956-59 (USLHS) vs 1954-59 (New England Lighthouses). The NRHP statement that the name was changed to 'New London Harbor Lighthouse' looks garbled and was left out; renaming comes from LighthouseFriends. The 1900 Light-House Board passage was read from OCR (scan page 75); printed page not confirmed. The 1900 report's own $60,000 revised estimate is OCR-garbled and was not used. Ernie ghost legend is presented only as legend. LighthouseFriends facts (1904-1907 acts, tow date, costs, 1981 rescue) rest on its cited reports/newspapers, not read directly. Beebe's account is from New England Lighthouses quoting the Providence Journal. The 1938 Bulletin passage is column-interleaved OCR. Tours: an event listing said they were cancelled; the Heritage Park page says June-September; verify. Roster stints parsed from roster.py output; Coast Guard crew named only as the archive prints them. Fact-check 2026-10-22: story edited for 'painted red' (NRHP) rather than red-brick, crib wording (NRHP says crib removed 1938), cost attribution, Beebe role disagreement (USLHS first assistant vs NEL principal keeper), log-entry author disagreement (LF Grace vs NLMS unknown), renaming date (NLMS 1910).
